output.title: Rest Day and Recovery
output.description: Process: Complete rest day with light foam rolling or passive mobility. Overall: Full recovery day to begin Week 11 and absorb the recent aerobic volume. Reason: Preserves structural and systemic energy before the mid-week quality and strength stimulus. Benefit: Restores glycogen, decreases connective tissue strain, and promotes parasympathetic nervous system tone. Warning: Avoid any cross-training or unscheduled jogging to ensure fresh legs.

output.title: Easy Aerobic Run with Flat Strides
output.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy aerobic running @ Zone 1-2 → 35 min steady Zone 2 running → 6 x 20s flat strides with 60s walking recovery → cool down 4 min easy jog. Overall: An aerobic maintenance session finished with flat strides to maintain top-end turnover without hills. Reason: Keeps neuromuscular pathways sharp while respecting flat terrain constraints. Benefit: Improves running economy, recruits high-threshold motor units, and builds aerobic capacity without metabolic fatigue. Warning: Do not turn strides into all-out straining sprints; focus on relaxed mechanics, tall posture, and quick ground contact.

output.title: Controlled Zone 3 Tempo Intervals
output.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy jogging @ Zone 1-2 → 3 x 10 min @ Zone 3 (4:45/km, 150-162 bpm), 3 min walking recovery → cool down 11 min easy jog. Overall: High-volume sub-threshold tempo work executed entirely on flat terrain. Reason: Enhances lactate clearance speed and builds aerobic power without exceeding AnT (168 bpm). Benefit: Shifts the aerobic threshold rightward, letting you sustain faster paces at lower relative cardiac cost. Warning: Strictly respect the upper heart rate limit (162 bpm); creeping into Zone 4 defeats the aerobic capacity objective and generates excessive autonomic fatigue.

output.title: Home Muscular Endurance Progression
output.description: Process: Warm up 10 min easy dynamic aerobic mobility building to Zone 3 for the final 2 min → 10 floor get-ups and 10 burpees → Split Jump Squats: 4x10/leg at ~1 jump/s, 45s rest between sets → Squat Jumps: 4x10, 45s rest between sets → Box Step-Ups onto sturdy bench/chair: 4x10/leg, ~1 rep/s, 30s rest between sets → Front Lunges: 4x10/leg, ~1 rep/s, 30s rest between sets → Cool down 10 min light walking and passive stretching. Overall: Targeted home-based Muscular Endurance circuit addressing chassis fatigue resistance for mountain running. Reason: Compensates for flat geography and lack of gym by stressing the quads and glutes with high local tension. Benefit: Increases muscular mitochondrial density, enhances local fatigue resistance, and bulletproofs knees and quads for the 2500m race descent. Warning: Focus strictly on controlled landing mechanics; if severe quadriceps burn causes form breakdown or knee valgus, extend the rest interval by 15 seconds.

output.title: Rest and Mobility
output.description: Process: Complete rest day with light foam rolling or passive mobility. Overall: Scheduled rest day providing recovery after Thursday's muscular endurance stimulus. Reason: Allows musculoskeletal remodeling and peripheral replenishment before the weekend long aerobic effort. Benefit: Lowers systemic inflammation, restores glycogen levels, and prepares connective tissue for endurance load. Warning: Do not substitute running or heavy strength work today; complete rest is mandatory.

output.title: Specific Mountain Long Run Simulation
output.fueling_tip: Consume 45-60g carbohydrates per hour (gels/chews) paired with 400-600ml water and 300-500mg sodium per hour.
output.description: Process: Warm up 15 min easy Zone 1 jogging → 105 min steady Zone 2 running at conversational effort → cool down 15 min walking and easy jog. Overall: Cornerstone aerobic endurance session building fat oxidation and mental resilience for 50K racing. Reason: Develops steady-state peripheral endurance, capillary density, and tests continuous multi-hour fueling strategies. Benefit: Enhances mitochondrial density in slow-twitch fibers and trains gut absorption under cumulative fatigue. Warning: Do not run fast to make up for flat terrain; maintain disciplined Zone 2 heart rate strictly below 148 bpm throughout.

output.title: Aerobic Flush and Recovery Run
output.fueling_tip: Plain water with optional electrolytes (200-400mg sodium); exogenous carbohydrates not required.
output.description: Process: Warm up 5 min brisk walk → 35 min easy Zone 1 jogging → cool down 5 min walking and mobility. Overall: Low-intensity aerobic recovery jog to close out Week 11. Reason: Promotes active circulation and clears metabolic waste without placing mechanical strain on tired tissues. Benefit: Accelerates systemic recovery while accumulating steady base volume below AeT. Warning: Keep the effort strictly in Zone 1; walk any slight rise if heart rate drifts toward 130 bpm.
